subject: Regional failover & burst capacity addendum
messages:

Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation — APAC rollout, EU residency + failover questions

Hi Laura,

Hope you're well — with your current subscription coming up for renewal in July, I wanted to start a quick thread to capture the changes we discussed on the last call: 1) DataClinic's APAC rollout timeline (targeting Aug–Sep) and 2) EU-only data residency for EU traffic plus an automated cross-region failover for DR.

Two asks to get us moving: can you confirm (a) whether APAC traffic must be strictly stored in APAC regions, and (b) the expected burst throughput for the first 90 days post-rollout (we need a baseline to size dedicated capacity).

I'll attach a draft SOW that includes an optional APAC burst addendum and a proposed failover SLA. Marissa (cc'd) will follow up on the technical-side details.

Thanks — I can hop on a call this week if you prefer to walk through the options.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0142 | dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the heads up. Quick answers from my side:
- APAC requirement: yes — patient data originating from our Singapore operations must remain in APAC (we have local PII rules).
- Burst plan: initial estimate is 3x baseline for first 90 days while we seed new services.

Procurement is on cc and will need the commercial terms + any amendments to data retention and residency spelled out. Also looping in Michael (Ops) for networking questions.

Can Marissa provide the failover behavior (RPO/RTO expectations) and whether the EU residency clause can be enforced at the request-routing level rather than object-level rehydration?

Laura Chen
Head of Cloud Engineering, DataClinic Health

Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — APAC rollout, EU residency + failover questions

Laura — thanks, got it.

Attached is a slightly updated SOW that includes two pricing lines: reserved capacity for EU (pinned residency) and an optional APAC burst pool sized at 3x baseline for the first 90 days. Also included is a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestone dates so procurement can see deliverables tied to payments.

If acceptable, we can: 1) add an EU Residency Addendum to the MSAs that enforces routing + storage in the EU region for EU-origin traffic, and 2) include an APAC Burst Addendum with a temporary burst multiplier and associated SLA credits if we miss the burst capacity SLOs.

Marissa — can you confirm the technical approach (routing affinity and incremental KV-cache warming) and if network egress/VPC peering requirements are covered in the diagram?

Next steps: I'll update the SOW redlines based on Procurement's feedback and put the final package into DocuSign once we confirm the residency language.

Best,
Dylan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 10:27:05 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — technical details on failover & residency

Thanks for looping me in. Short technical notes to make sure expectations align:

- Residency enforcement: We can enforce EU residency at the request-routing layer using geo-ip + token-claim checks. For long-term cold storage, we recommend setting a policy to keep EU-origin artifacts in EU buckets by default; object-level rehydration would be a separate workflow and not automatic during failover.

- Failover behavior: We support active-to-active for read traffic with per-request region affinity. For full region failover (e.g., EU -> APAC), the platform will fail over new write sessions to the next region but does not automatically backfill warm KV state unless you opt into the KV-replication addon (this is what preserves low-latency state after failover). RPO with KV-replication: ~10s; without: best-effort (minutes). RTO: experimental path we can commit to 5–10 minutes for routing, longer for full-state rehydration.

- Networking: VPC peering and private-link options are in the diagram. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) in both EU and APAC.

I'll edit the SOW section to call out the KV-replication option and measurable RPO/RTO in the addendum. Open to a quick call to walk Michael through the diagram.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Appreciate the detail — that helps. Procurement attached a short security questionnaire we need you to complete (I attached it here). A couple of redlines from our legal/ops teams:
- We need the EU Residency Addendum to explicitly state that EU-origin PII will not be replicated to APAC without a documented exception and signed agreement.
- For the APAC burst pool, we want a one-time 30% renewal credit applied if Redwood misses the agreed burst SLO in the first 90 days.

Also, can you confirm support for BYOK in the proposed EU residency flow?

I'll flag anything else after procurement has a chance to review the SOW.

Laura

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, procurement@dataclinic.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — commercial response and next steps

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear asks and for raising the redlines. I'm looping in to propose a concise commercial path so we can close the renewal on time:

1) EU Residency Addendum: we will add explicit language preventing automatic replication of EU-origin PII to APAC. Any replication to APAC will require a signed exception and an audit record. BYOK is supported for EU-region keys; we'll include KMS integration notes in the addendum.

2) APAC Burst SLA concession: Redwood will include a one-time 30% credit if we fail to meet the agreed burst capacity SLO in the first 90 days. The SLO will be tied to a measurable throughput metric in the MAP.

3) KV-replication: to meet the RPO/RTO you outlined, we recommend the KV-replication addon for the APAC rollout window. Commercially, we'll discount the first 3 months of the addon by 15% to help with cutover risk.

4) Next steps: Dylan will incorporate the exact legal language into the SOW and route the package to DocuSign. If procurement is ready, we can target signature by 2027-06-18 to preserve current pricing and ensure APAC capacity reservation for Aug.

Laura — if that plan looks acceptable, Dylan will send the redlined SOW today. Happy to join the signature call if needed.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Commercial | Redwood Inference
